chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: The Jelly Roll Morton sessions: personnel and arrangements
summary: Personnel included Bechet, Albert Nicholas, Sidney DeParis and Zutty Singleton; Jelly wrote out the arrangements for his numbers.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: I've got all -- I think I've got that date them all. But what do you remember about days with Jelly? How did that go? I mean you'd got -- I mean you'd got Bechet on there too. One of the
One of the records -- this one that he gave me with these four taken for the master record was recorded, was taken off in France. Bechet wasn't on that

date. It was nothing but Albert Nicholas, myself, Sidney DeParis, Freddy -- oh, used to be with Louie and did a lot of recording with Jelly in Chicago -- Freddy Robinson was on trombone. And Jug -- not Jug on piano -- and William Brault Brothers on bass, and Sidney DeParis on trumpet. But when we made the big recordings, which had happened in 1939, this was recorded again in September, and we carved it in round about July, and that's when we had Bechet, Albert Nicholas, Sidney DeParis, and the whole eight -- whole nine of us was on that group, whole eight of us on that group. Zutty was on all of those, though, with Jelly.
Well, how did that session go?
Very nice, because Jelly arranged us on the last big ones we made, Jelly made the arrangements for those numbers because a lot of them was his.
Well, I mean did he write these things out or were they sort of oral
Yeah, well, I mean, you know --
